sources.citation: Cloarec-Heiss, France. 1986. Dynamique et équilibre d'une syntaxe: le banda-linda de Centrafrique. Paris: SELAF. Introduction A. Situation
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.103.13.4 (2); Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8051.Z9 L563 1986); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.103.13.4 (2); Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8051.Z9 L563 1986
sources.note: Mentions 'les Lagba, Gbaga, Buka et Yangere qui vivent en milieu gbaya en Centrafrique ouest et sud-ouest' as a fraction detached from the main Banda group; the grammar is Linda, not Yangere; Gallica full-text search for 'accent' in the book = 0 hits.

sources.citation: Diki-Kidiri, Marcel & France Cloarec-Heiss. 1985. Précis d'orthographe banda. Colloque sur la création de systèmes orthographiques en Afrique centrale, Université de Bangui, 16-25 avril 1985. Bangui: Institut de Linguistique Appliquée. 13 pp. (SIL Language and Culture Archives copy; pan-Banda, examples from linda, ndokpa, tangbago; Yangere not named)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No accent/stress statement. PDF p. 2 (précis p. 1) sec. 1.1: 'Toutes les variétés de banda recensées font usage de trois tons ponctuels (haut, moyen, bas) et de deux tons modulés (descendant et montant).' Sec. 1.2: syllables V, CV, CVV, no closed syllables. Group-level, not Yangere-specific.

sources.citation: Tisserant, Charles. 1930. Essai sur la grammaire banda. Paris: Institut d'ethnologie (Travaux et mémoires 13). Multidialectal (Togbo/Linda area)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.105.23 (13); Widener Library, call number Sci 3080.87 vol.13)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.105.23 (13); Widener Library, call number Sci 3080.87 vol.13
sources.note: Only names Yangere as a Banda tribe ('les Yangere (Yanguéré) sur la Sanga (?)', p. 6; 'infiltrations, au Sud-Ouest, jusqu'à la Sangha (Yanguéré)', p. 3). Its accent passage (pp. 23-24: three tones plus an 'accent d'intensité' whose position is not stated) is not about Yangere.

sources.citation: Moéhama, Elisée. 2021. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: Première évaluation parmi les Yangere. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-024. Dallas: SIL International. 52 pp. (SIL RCA fieldwork 20-25 Nov 1995)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey only (RTT intelligibility with Linda/Mono/Ngbugu, Sango SRT, vitality); the words ton/tonal/accent/stress do not occur. Reproduces Cloarec-Heiss 1988: 59-60 / Moñino 1988: 19 classification (yangere = Banda central, group 7) and ALAC 1984: 43 ('groupe qui semble assez différencié.. îlot en pays gbaya').

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed. Entry Banda-Yangere [yaj] (Internet Archive copy 2016-03-05)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing linguistic. Population 26,500 (1996); Bambio, Berbérati, Carnot subprefectures, some in Nola; 'Writing: Unwritten'.

sources.citation: Bluhberger, Jutta. 2011/2021. SIL Banda survey reports (Linda SILESR 2011-001; Moruba JLSR 2021-013; Gbambiya 2021-014; Mbres 2021-031); Althabegoity, Léa. 2024. Étude des verbes en ngbugu (thèse, HAL tel-05023143)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Yangere appears only in classification tables and intelligibility remarks (Ngbugu speaker AOS8 reports 'des difficultés à comprendre les parlers yangere et linda') and in one thesis footnote (verb da 'se battre' attested in yangere). No Yangere phonology; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & M. A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: OUP for IAI. Banda-Gbaya-Ngbandi languages, sec. 2 'Tone and Stress' (Google Books preview page of the 2017 Routledge reprint)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Group-level only, no Yangere data: 2a 'There appear to be three main tone levels in these languages -- High, Mid, and Low.' 2b 'Stress is often responsible for changes in vowel quality and vowel length.. In NGBAKA, GBAYA, and BANDA, on the other hand, there is a tendency towards extra shortness here [the penultimate syllable]. Compare Eboué's BANDA spellings yaUra (dog), yabru (goat), akblo (child) with Hackett's TOGBO renderings yavóró, abòrò, àgbòlò.' No stress-position rule.
